name: Pituitary Hormone Deficiency of Tumoral Origin
aliases: Secondary Hypopituitarism due to Pituitary Tumor

criteria.description: Demonstration of deficiency in one or more anterior pituitary hormones (e.g., ACTH, TSH, GH, LH/FSH, prolactin)
Radiological evidence of pituitary or hypothalamic tumor on MRI or CT scan
Presence of clinical signs and symptoms consistent with hypopituitarism (e.g., secondary adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism, hypogonadism)
Exclusion of primary pituitary or hypothalamic disorders unrelated to tumor

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pituitary hormone deficiency confirmed biochemically plus imaging evidence of a pituitary or hypothalamic tumor with compatible clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Dynamic hormone testing may be required to confirm deficiencies; tumor size and location influence clinical presentation.

common.notes: Leads to decreased muscle mass and altered lipid metabolism

common.symptomName: Headache due to tumor mass effect
searchTerms: pain from brain tumor mass effect
visual field cuts on both sides
low blood sodium from cortisol deficiency
low sodium levels due to hormone imbalance
low sex drive and trouble conceiving
difficulty with sexual function and fertility
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

rare.notes: Rare complication from tumor mass effect

laboratory: Low serum cortisol with low or inappropriately normal ACTH
Low free T4 with low or normal TSH
Low serum IGF-1 indicating growth hormone deficiency
Low LH and FSH with low sex steroids
Hyponatremia due to secondary adrenal insufficiency
imaging: MRI showing pituitary macroadenoma or other sellar/suprasellar mass
Compression or displacement of optic chiasm
genetic: No specific genetic mutations directly associated; genetic testing may be indicated if familial tumor syndromes suspected
other: Dynamic endocrine testing (e.g., insulin tolerance test, ACTH stimulation test) to confirm hormone deficiencies
Visual field testing for optic chiasm compression

distinguishingFeatures: Possible autoimmune or infiltrative pituitary disease
Acute onset with severe headache and visual loss

redFlags: Sudden severe headache with visual loss
Rapid onset of adrenal crisis symptoms
references: Melmed S. Pituitary Tumors. N Engl J Med. 2020;382(10):937-950.
Orphanet: Pituitary hormone deficiency of tumoral origin - ORPHA:95503
